title: Sources and drivers of antibiotic resistance genes across rivers and lakes
desc: River and lake ecosystems are important reservoirs and transmission pathways for antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), yet the global distribution, sources and risks of their resistomes remain poorly understood. Here we analysed 4,128 river and lake metagenomes (water and sediment) from 42 countries and regions and constructed a comprehensive genome-resolved catalogue of ARG-carrying bacteria, revealing key pathogenic vectors of resistance. Clinically important ARGs, including blaOXA and mcr, were widespread and showed distinct biogeographical patterns, highlighting rivers and lakes as potential sentinels for global antimicrobial resistance surveillance. Here, using an integrative source-tracking framework, we identified aquaculture, hospital sewage and municipal sewage as major contributors to riverine resistomes, with the estimated contribution of aquaculture increasing from 11% in 2012 to 40% in 2020. Human population and aquaculture intensity emerged as key drivers of the distribution and associated risks of river and lake resistomes. We further generated a predictive global map of freshwater resistome risk. By transforming metagenomic data into a tool for tracing antimicrobial resistance, our study establishes rivers as potential early-warning systems and supports their integration into One Health surveillance frameworks. A comprehensive analysis of river and lake resistomes reveals the growing contribution of aquaculture to antimicrobial resistance in rivers and offers insights to strengthen environmental surveillance and early-warning systems.

title: Ebola virus-based antibody products cross-neutralize 2026 Bundibugyo virus glycoprotein
desc: The ongoing 2026 outbreak of Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) disease has highlighted the urgent need for therapeutic countermeasures. Whether Ebola virus (EBOV)-induced antibodies can cross-neutralize contemporary BDBVs is unclear. Here we test a diverse panel of EBOV-derived polyclonal and monoclonal antibodies, including plasma from humans after EBOV infection and horse plasma and mice serum immunized with available EBOV immunogens, against vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV) pseudotypes presenting BDBV-2026 glycoprotein (GP). We find that all antibodies retain cross-neutralizing activity against BDBV-2026 glycoprotein. These findings identify existing Ebola virus-derived antibody preparations as candidates for rapid evaluation. Antibodies raised by Ebola virus retain neutralizing activity against the glycoprotein of the Bundibugyo virus causing the 2026 outbreak, supporting the rapid evaluation of existing Ebola antibody products in the current outbreak.
